transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Well, I don’t want to make too much of it, Doctor, but… things have gotten pretty hard since they changed my hours at the warehouse and brought in this new inventory system. I used to manage alright, but lately I feel like I’m sort of falling apart.

I’ve missed some shifts, and even some church commitments, which isn’t like me. I’ve been short with my family too, snapping when I don’t mean to. Some mornings I get my work boots on and then just sit there, wondering if I can even face going in. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… that’s why I came.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I guess it’s been about five months now, if I’m counting right. It started around when they changed the warehouse schedule and brought in that new inventory system. I kept thinking I’d adjust to it, you know, but… it’s been hanging on longer than I expected.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, like activities or time with family and friends?

I’m not sure I’d say I don’t enjoy them, exactly. I mean… I still care about my family and church and all that. Maybe I’m just not as easy in myself lately, so it’s harder to settle into things the way I used to. But I don’t know if that counts as not enjoying them, Doctor.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or blaming yourself for things more than usual?

I don’t think so… not in a big way, anyway. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I don’t handle things the way I should, but I wouldn’t say I sit around thinking I’m no good or anything like that.

Maybe I’m a little harder on myself than usual, but… I don’t know. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual or, on the contrary, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

I don’t think I’ve noticed that, no. I mean, I may be a little slower getting going some days, but I’m 74, so I don’t know what’s normal and what’s not anymore. I wouldn’t say I’m pacing around or can’t sit still or anything like that. Does that answer it okay?

Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately—like not being able to fall asleep, waking up during the night, or waking up earlier than you should? Or on the other hand, have you found yourself sleeping much more than usual?

I’m not really sure, Doctor. I mean, I don’t think I’m sleeping a whole lot more or anything like that. Some nights aren’t perfect, but at my age I sort of expect that, you know?

I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. I can usually get some sleep. Is that helpful?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately—like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?

I don’t think so, not really. My appetite’s maybe not what it used to be, but I haven’t noticed anything dramatic, and I’m not trying to lose weight or anything.

I guess I still eat enough. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Doctor: Have you had days where you felt down or hopeless most of the time, nearly every day, for a period of at least a couple of weeks?

I don’t think I’d say hopeless, no. I mean, I’ve had some low days, sure, but not like being down most of the day every day for two weeks straight. At least I don’t think so.

I don’t want to overstate it. I’m trying to answer it the right way—does that make sense?
Have you had times where you felt down or sad for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

I’m not sure I’d put it that strongly. I mean, I’ve been sad here and there, and some days feel heavier than others, but most of the day, nearly every day, for two weeks straight… I don’t think so.

I hope that’s a clear enough answer.
Have you found that you take less pleasure or interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies, church activities, or spending time with family?

I’m not sure. I mean, I still do things with the family and that sort of thing. Maybe I’m not as eager about some things as I used to be, but I wouldn’t say I’ve completely lost interest.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean. I’m trying not to make it sound worse than it is.
Have you had a period lasting at least two weeks where most days you felt down or sad for most of the day, even if you couldn’t put your finger on why?

I don’t think so, not for two weeks like that. I’ve had stretches where I felt kind of low or off, but saying most of the day, most days… I’m not sure that would be accurate.

I mean, maybe I’ve had days where I couldn’t quite explain why I felt sad, but I don’t think it lasted in that steady way you’re describing. Does that answer it okay?
Have you had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or sad for most of the day, nearly every day, even if it wasn’t tied to anything specific happening?

I don’t think I’ve had it that steady, no. I mean, I’ve had bad days, sure, and sometimes I feel pretty low for a while, but the “most of the day, nearly every day for two weeks” part… I don’t think I can honestly say that.

I hope I’m answering what you’re asking.
